Different sensitivity of items to hash collisions. In other words, items with different frequency ranges have different sensitivities to hash collisions. We choose CM, Cold Filter (CF) [48] and Elastic sketch (Elastic) [39] as representatives of different types of sketches. We set parameters as their original papers recommend and conduct an experiment on estimating item frequency using these sketches on the CAIDA dataset. Due to space limitation, we do not show the results on other datasets, which are similar to the results on the CAIDA dataset. Figure 3 shows the average relative errors (ARE) of estimates in different frequency intervals. The results indicate that for items with the frequency interval of (1, 10], (100, 1000] and (10000, MAX], the ARE falls within the range of (10−2 ,104 ), (10−4 ,102 ) and (10−7 ,10−1 ), respectively. We intuitively discover that items with different frequencies tolerate estimate errors of different orders of magnitude. The root cause of this gap is their varying levels of sensitivity to hash collisions. Specifically, cold items are the most sensitive to hash collisions, followed by warm items and hot items. Due to the small frequency of cold items and their hash collisions with non-cold items, their estimated value is much larger than the true frequency, resulting in a large error.
